extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of theology/divinity; clergy and educated Christian readers
extracted.subtask_description: Close doctrinal commentary on biblical concepts: the kingdom of God, holiness, sacraments, the Word of God, and the nature and modes of prophets. The text explicates definitions, senses, and canonical examples from Scripture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kingdome of God — civil commonwealth interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kingdome of God is a Civill Kingdome, instituted (by the consent of those which were to be subject thereto) for their Civill Government, and the regulating of their behaviour, not onely towards God their King, but also towards one another in point of justice, and towards other Nations both in peace and warre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Kingdome is a real earthly kingdom in which God is King and the High Priest his viceroy; the Old Testament and New Testament passages (e.g., 1 Sam. 8.7; Isaiah 24.23; Luke 1.32,33) are read to support a literal, civil sense of God's reign and its restoration by Christ. The Lord's Prayer ('Thy Kingdome come') thus refers to the restoration of this civil-theocratic order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation nuance — 'Sacerdotall Kingdome' vs 'Kingdome of Priests'
rubrics_metrics.description: The text notes the Latin 'Regnum Sacerdotale' and English renderings such as 'a Kingdome of Priests' or 'a Regal Priesthood', and argues these translations affect meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing 'Kingdome of Priests' versus 'Sacerdotall Kingdome' shifts the interpretation and has ecclesiastical-political consequences (it lightens or obscures claims to ecclesiastical government by Christian kings). Translational choices should be weighed for their doctrinal and institutional implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holy — defined as God's propriety (special right)
rubrics_metrics.description: Holy signifieth, that which is Gods by speciall, not by generall Right. All the Earth is God's, but only that which is set apart for his especiall service is called Holy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Sabbath (God's day) is Holy, the Temple a Holy House, Sacrifices/Tithes Holy Duties, Priests/Prophets/Anointed Kings Holy Men. 'Holy' properly implies propriety acquired by covenant or consecration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profane/Common — opposite of holy
rubrics_metrics.description: The word Profane is usually taken in the Scripture for the same with Common; and consequently their contraries, Holy, and Proper, in the Kingdome of God must be the same also.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Profane’/‘common’ denotes what is not specially appropriated to God or public (the kingly) service; treat 'holy' and 'public' as analogous legal-proprietary categories within theocratic polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degrees of Sanctity
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Holinesse there be degrees: the whole nation of Israelites were Holy to God; the tribe of Levi was a Holy tribe; amongst the Levites, the Priests were yet more Holy; amongst the Priests, the High Priest was the most Holy. Likewise land/city/temple/sanctum had ascending holiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctity is hierarchical and relative: things or persons set apart for nearer or more especial service gain higher degrees of holiness; this principle guides allocation of roles and access (e.g., only the High Priest entered the Sanctum Sanctorum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacrament — separation and consecration; admission vs commemoration
rubrics_metrics.description: A SACRAMENT, is a separation of some visible thing from common use; and a consecration of it to Gods service, for a sign, either of our admission into the Kingdome of God, or for a Commemoration of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal sacraments of Admission: Circumcision (Old), Baptisme (New) — used once. Principal sacraments of Commemoration: Passover (Old), Lord's Supper (New) — to be reiterated. Other consecrations exist but, insofar as a sacrament implies an oath/promise of allegiance, only the listed rites function as sacraments in that strict sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word of God — defined as Speech/Discourse (Sermo/Logos)
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is mention of the Word of God, it doth not signifie a part of Speech... but a perfect Speech or Discourse, whereby the speaker Affirmeth, Denieth, Commandeth, Promiseth, Threateneth, Wisheth, or Interrogateth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat 'word' as Sermo/Logos — a propositional, communicative act — not merely an isolated vocable; this affects interpretation of scriptural 'words' and theological claims about revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word of God — two principal senses: spoken by God vs concerning God (doctrine)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Words Spoken By God And Concerning God, Both Are Called Gods Word In Scripture. It may be understood sometimes of the Speaker (the words that God hath spoken) and sometimes of the Subject (the doctrine concerning God).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Word of God' used for Gospel doctrine (Acts 13.46) as well as for divine utterances to prophets; in Greek usage Logos Theou can mean Theologia. Keep these senses distinct when attributing authority or inferring audible speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word of God — as effect or the thing promised
rubrics_metrics.description: For the effect of his Word; that is to say, for the thing it self, which by his Word is Affirmed, Commanded, Threatned, or Promised (e.g., 'till his Word was come' means till that which was foretold came to pass).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scriptural 'word' can denote the fulfillment or event promised; interpret prophetic statements both as speech-acts and as promises whose realization is part of their identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word of God — also signifying words consonant to reason and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: There are also places of the Scripture, where, by the Word of God, is signified such Words as are consonant to reason, and equity, though spoken sometimes neither by prophet, nor by a holy man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrinally, some 'words of God' are identified with natural reason or equity (written in men's hearts); be open to reading prudential or rational counsel as fitting under divine speech in certain scriptural contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophet — multiple acceptions (prolocutor, praedictor, incoherent speaker)
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of PROPHET signifieth sometimes Prolocutor (he that speaketh from God to Man), sometimes Praedictor (a foreteller of things to come), and sometimes one that speaketh incoherently (as men that are distracted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize functional variety: prophets can be spokesmen (Moses, Samuel), intercessors (Abraham called a prophet for praying), singers/praisers (Miriam), or teachers in congregations (1 Cor. 14.3). Context determines which sense is operative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Praediction of future contingents — not always prophecy (impostors and non-constant vocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: When by Prophecy is meant Praediction... not only they were Prophets who were Gods spokesmen, but also all those Imposters that pretend by the helpe of familiar spirits... to foretell events; Prophecy is not an art, nor a constant Vocation, but an extraordinary, and temporary Employment from God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish true prophetic vocation (extraordinary divine commission) from imposture, chance hits, or arts of divination; beware that false prophets may gain reputation from occasional successes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner in which God hath spoken to Prophets — modes enumerated
rubrics_metrics.description: God made his presence manifest by Apparition, Vision, Dream, voice from heaven, and special modes for Moses ('mouth to mouth'); to extraordinary prophets usually in Dreams or Visions; to Moses more cleerly; to High Priests from the Mercy Seat; in the New Testament also by Visions and Dreams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scriptural markers (visions, dreams, audible voice, apparition) to identify mode of revelation; Moses and the High Priest occupy a distinct, higher category of address whose exact manner is 'not intelligible' but treated as exceptional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate/perpetual prophets — 'speaking by the Spirit' as moral/inclining operation
rubrics_metrics.description: To subordinate Prophets of perpetuall Calling, I find not any place that proveth God spake to them supernaturally; but onely in such manner, as naturally he inclineth men to Piety, to Beleef, to Righteousnesse... 'spoke by the Spirit' means speaking according to God's will, declared by the supreme Prophet; the Spirit signifieth Mind and Disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret 'spirit' in such contexts as moral inclination or grace aiding obedience, not necessarily as direct supernatural revelation or indwelling of Divine nature (contrast with Christ).

rubrics_metrics.name: God sometimes spake by Lots
rubrics_metrics.description: God spake also many times by the event of Lots; which were ordered by such as he had put in Authority over his people (e.g., Saul's drawing of lots to reveal Jonathan's fault; Joshua casting lots to divide the land).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occurrences of lot-drawing are treated as modes by which divine will was manifested through instituted procedures; include such events among legitimate scriptural modes of divine communication.
